questions.stem: A patient who had a heart attack last year takes a high-intensity statin. Their low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol is 88 mg/dL. Is this at goal?

options.text: Yes, cholesterol goals are no longer used
No, the goal is below 70, or below 55 if very high risk

questions.explanation: C is correct: after a heart attack, the goal is below 70, or below 55 if very high risk; 88 is above both. A uses the goal for adults 40 to 75 with diabetes. B is wrong because goals are back in 2026. D is not the goal taught.

questions.stem: Which statin regimens are high intensity? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: B, D, and F are correct: high intensity is atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg. A, simvastatin 40, and E, pravastatin 80, are moderate intensity; only atorvastatin and rosuvastatin reach high intensity. C, rosuvastatin 10, is in the moderate range of 5 to 10.

questions.stem: A patient had a stroke from blocked arteries 3 months ago and is starting a statin. Which regimen is best?
questions.explanation: D is correct: after a stroke from blocked arteries, the patient needs a high-intensity statin, and rosuvastatin 20 is high intensity. A, B, and C are moderate intensity.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old with diabetes and no heart disease is starting a statin. What fits the 2026 guideline taught?

options.text: At least a moderate-intensity statin, with an LDL goal below 100
No statin until a heart attack occurs
Diet only; statins are not used in diabetes

questions.explanation: A is correct: adults 40 to 75 with diabetes get at least a moderate-intensity statin, with a goal below 100. B waits for an event the statin is meant to prevent. C is the goal for very high risk after a heart attack, stroke, or blocked arteries. D is wrong because statins are recommended for this age group with diabetes.

questions.stem: A patient with a past heart attack takes atorvastatin 80 mg every day as prescribed. LDL is still above goal. What is the next step?
questions.explanation: D is correct: once a high-intensity statin is confirmed and taken, add ezetimibe. A switches to a moderate-intensity statin, which lowers LDL less. C removes the main heart protection. B also lowers LDL less.

questions.stem: A patient on a statin reports new muscle weakness and dark urine. What is the best action?

options.text: Continue the statin and add a pain reliever
Stop the statin and check creatine kinase
Switch the dose to the morning

questions.explanation: C is correct: weakness and dark urine suggest rare muscle breakdown, so stop the statin and check creatine kinase. A keeps the drug that may be causing the damage. B makes muscle injury more likely. D changes timing but leaves the muscle breakdown untreated.

questions.stem: A patient on simvastatin is prescribed clarithromycin. What is the best action?

options.text: Do not combine them; hold the statin or choose another antibiotic

questions.explanation: D is correct: simvastatin must not be combined with strong liver-enzyme blockers like clarithromycin. A misses a serious interaction. B raises the simvastatin level even more. C changes timing but does not stop the enzyme block.

questions.stem: Which statins are much less affected by drugs that block their liver enzyme? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: B, D, and E are correct: rosuvastatin, pravastatin, and pitavastatin are much less affected. A, simvastatin, and C, lovastatin, are broken down by the liver enzyme that many drugs block, so their levels rise a lot.

questions.stem: Which statin is best taken in the evening?

options.text: None; timing matters for every statin equally

questions.explanation: C is correct: short-acting simvastatin is best taken in the evening. A and B work any time of day. D is wrong because atorvastatin and rosuvastatin work any time, while simvastatin is best in the evening.

questions.stem: How much does a moderate-intensity statin lower LDL cholesterol?
questions.explanation: A is correct: moderate intensity lowers LDL by 30% to 49%. B is high intensity. C and D are smaller than either intensity level.
